correctness.rationale: All quantifiers are explicit: n>=3, all weights positive, all p,q>=1, arbitrary nonlinear exact isometries. Equality in a trace norm metric segment reduces every vertex to a positive factor under one polar partial isometry. Pairwise singleton distances give orthogonal positive supports; distances from every vertex to its active singletons imply PSD domination; trace equality rules out off-support and off-block terms. This reconstructs every image, proves a complex-linear isometric extension, and gives the sharp rank obstruction rank(top-bottom)>=n. Two-sided orthonormal-frame constructions prove existence whenever min(p,q)>=n. Finite checker: 104261 passed diagnostics; universal claims do not depend on finite tests.

value.rationale: The full weighted Boolean cube is a canonical finite metric family. An all-embeddings theorem determining exact matrix rank and forcing complex-linear extension from a nonlinear metric sample gives substantive rigidity unavailable from mere existence tests. Orthogonal positive supports provide a complete representation across continuous weights and every rectangular size; minimum-size configurations are classified. No downstream theorem is needed for the natural classification to be valuable.
